title: Who Should Build the Low-Carbon Economy?
gist: Clean-energy deployment is globalizing while the capacity to invent and manufacture the technology stays clustered in five economies: 60-85% of most clean-energy supply-chain capacity sits in no more than five countries and 92% of 2023 climate-tech patents came from China, Japan, South Korea, the US, and the EU. The author argues the low-carbon transition is replicating the industrial era's concentration of value capture, and that the Belém Technology Implementation Programme's push for domestic innovation — not just technology transfer — is the corrective.

insights.claim: Across most clean-energy supply chains, 60-85% of production capacity sits in no more than five countries, and some individual segments exceed 95%.
insights.speaker: PEDRO IVO FERRAZ DA SILVA
insights.so_what: Extreme supply-chain concentration is a standing tail risk for energy-transition capex: a single-country export control or tariff action can reprice entire clean-tech project pipelines.
insights.quote: Across most clean-energy supply chains, 60-85% of production capacity is concentrated in no more than five countries, with some individual segments exceeding 95%.

insights.claim: Global solar capacity has increased tenfold since 2015 even as manufacturing capability remained highly concentrated, showing deployment and production geography can decouple entirely.
insights.speaker: PEDRO IVO FERRAZ DA SILVA
insights.so_what: Demand growth in solar does not translate into local manufacturing equity value — the profit pool stays with incumbent producers, favoring existing scaled manufacturers over new-entrant national champions.
insights.quote: solar capacity having increased tenfold since 2015

insights.claim: The IEA sees no major shift in the geography of clean-energy supply chains as likely before 2030, despite mounting diversification efforts.
insights.speaker: PEDRO IVO FERRAZ DA SILVA
insights.so_what: Sets a concrete horizon: friend-shoring and localization policies announced now should not be underwritten as delivering diversified capacity within this decade.
insights.quote: no major shift in these supply chains’ geography is likely before 2030
insights.locator: Despite mounting efforts to diversify production

insights.claim: Emerging clean-tech segments including electrolyzers for low-emissions hydrogen and small modular reactors are already displaying the same concentration dynamics as mature solar, wind, and battery supply chains.
insights.speaker: PEDRO IVO FERRAZ DA SILVA
insights.so_what: Bets on hydrogen or SMRs as a chance for new countries to enter the value chain are likely to disappoint; incumbency is forming early, so back the early leaders rather than the latecomers.
insights.quote: Emerging sectors such as electrolyzers for low-emissions hydrogen and small modular reactors are already exhibiting similar dynamics.
insights.locator: Worse, this trend is no longer confined

insights.claim: About 92% of patents for new environment- and climate-change-related technologies in 2023 came from just China, Japan, South Korea, the United States, and the European Union.
insights.speaker: PEDRO IVO FERRAZ DA SILVA
insights.so_what: Climate-tech IP rents accrue to five jurisdictions — a durable structural argument for owning the innovators rather than the adopters.
insights.quote: about 92% of the patents for new environment- and climate change-related technologies in 2023 stemmed from China, Japan, South Korea, the United States, and the European Union
insights.locator: Data collected by the OECD show

insights.claim: By the mid-1800s steam locomotives were operating in almost 60 countries or colonies while only Britain, the United States, and certain German states could actually supply them — the original template of global adoption with concentrated production.
insights.speaker: PEDRO IVO FERRAZ DA SILVA
insights.so_what: A reusable historical lens: in every technology wave, adoption breadth is a poor proxy for where returns land.
insights.quote: By the mid-1800s, steam locomotives were already operational in almost 60 countries or colonies, yet only Britain, the United States, and certain German states were fully capable of supplying them.

insights.claim: Of the large developing economies in Asia and Latin America that internationalized auto manufacturing after World War II, only Japan and South Korea graduated into the exclusive club of original equipment manufacturers.
insights.speaker: PEDRO IVO FERRAZ DA SILVA
insights.so_what: A base rate worth pricing: successful climbs from assembly to OEM status are extraordinarily rare, tempering optimism about industrial-policy catch-up stories.
insights.quote: only two of these economies, Japan and South Korea, managed to join the exclusive club of so-called original equipment manufacturers
insights.locator: especially in large developing countries in Asia and Latin America

insights.claim: The post-Cold War IT model captured by 'Designed in California, assembled in China' institutionalized a split between knowledge-intensive, well-paid work and labor-intensive, low-paid operations.
insights.speaker: PEDRO IVO FERRAZ DA SILVA
insights.so_what: The design/assembly margin split is the defining feature of modern supply chains — the analytical question for any new sector is which side of that line a country or company sits on.
insights.quote: drawing a clear line between knowledge-intensive, well-remunerated activities and labor-intensive, low-paid operational ones
insights.locator: With the end of the Cold War

insights.claim: China's rise in solar panels and wind turbines came through joint ventures and licensing agreements with advanced-economy providers, a learning blueprint analysts hoped other developing countries could copy via 'green windows of opportunity.'
insights.speaker: PEDRO IVO FERRAZ DA SILVA
insights.so_what: Names the specific mechanism of technological catch-up — JV plus licensing — which is precisely the channel now being closed off by export controls and trade barriers.
insights.locator: When China started to gain global market share

themes.theme: Contrarian read on the green transition

insights.claim: Rather than producing a more distributed industrial landscape, the low-carbon transition is reproducing the familiar pattern in which adoption is global but knowledge, productive capacity, and value creation stay clustered in very few countries.
insights.speaker: PEDRO IVO FERRAZ DA SILVA
insights.so_what: Directly contradicts the 'green leapfrogging' narrative used to justify emerging-market clean-tech industrial policy — a reason to discount those catch-up premiums.
insights.quote: adoption is global, but the knowledge, productive capacity, and value creation remain clustered in a remarkably small number of countries
insights.locator: Rather than ushering in a more distributed industrial

insights.claim: The geographical diversification of technological innovation has remained more of a dream than a reality despite a decade of clean-tech expansion.
insights.speaker: PEDRO IVO FERRAZ DA SILVA
insights.so_what: Sets expectations for COP-cycle diversification pledges: treat them as aspiration, not forecast.
insights.quote: the geographical diversification of technological innovation has remained more of a dream than a reality

themes.theme: Policy architecture: big push and Belém

insights.claim: The Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean argues a coordinated-investment 'big push' is required to transform productive structures and build domestic innovation capability in left-behind regions.
insights.speaker: PEDRO IVO FERRAZ DA SILVA
entities: Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean
insights.so_what: Signals the intellectual framing behind future Latin American industrial-policy and development-bank lending programs.
insights.quote: a “big push” will be necessary to mobilize the coordinated investments capable of transforming productive structures
insights.locator: The Economic Commission for Latin America

insights.claim: Parties to the Paris agreement adopted the Belém Technology Implementation Programme, whose pioneering feature is treating domestic innovation in developing countries as a requirement rather than accepting transfer of off-the-shelf technologies as sufficient.
insights.speaker: PEDRO IVO FERRAZ DA SILVA
entities: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
insights.so_what: A new multilateral channel that could push climate finance toward local R&D and manufacturing rather than equipment imports — relevant to development-bank and EPC contractor pipelines.
insights.quote: One pioneering feature of this program is that it frames domestic innovation as a must, rather than deeming the transfer of off-the-shelf technologies sufficient.
insights.locator: One pioneering feature of this program

insights.claim: Technology transfer should be redefined to occur across the whole innovation cycle — research, design, demonstration, deployment, and commercialization — instead of being confined to diffusion of fully mature solutions.
insights.speaker: PEDRO IVO FERRAZ DA SILVA
insights.so_what: If adopted in climate agreements, this reframing changes what counts as compliance and could shift where transition finance is spent.
insights.quote: transfers can take place across multiple stages of the innovation process
insights.locator: To be sure, technology transfer remains a cornerstone

insights.claim: Implementation of the Belém program will be obstructed by geopolitical tensions, trade barriers, and the diversion of financial resources toward security and defense.
insights.speaker: PEDRO IVO FERRAZ DA SILVA
insights.so_what: Explicitly names the defense-spending crowd-out of climate finance — a competing claim on the same fiscal pool that favors defense over climate budgets.
insights.quote: from geopolitical tensions and trade barriers to the diversion of financial resources toward security and defense
insights.locator: Implementation of the Belém program will face

insights.claim: Technologies are not universal: drawing on Yuk Hui's concept of 'cosmotechnics,' they carry the worldview and values of the places where they were conceived, so imported solutions fit context-specific problems poorly.
insights.speaker: PEDRO IVO FERRAZ DA SILVA
insights.so_what: An argument for localized product design in emerging markets — relevant to whether standardized Western or Chinese clean-tech hardware wins developing-market tenders.
insights.quote: They carry the worldview and values of the places where they were conceived.

insights.claim: The success of the low-carbon transition should be measured not only by the speed at which technologies spread but by how widely the capabilities to innovate, adapt, and produce them are distributed.
insights.speaker: PEDRO IVO FERRAZ DA SILVA
insights.so_what: A proposed alternative KPI for the transition; if it gains traction in UNFCCC processes it reshapes what climate programs are funded and judged on.
insights.quote: The success of the low-carbon transition should not be measured only by the speed at which technologies spread, but also by how widely the capabilities to innovate, adapt, and produce them are distributed.
